answer: In PoA, each identity must lock bonded collateral in an escrow, so splitting influence does not remove accountability. If k identities coordinate an equivocation, correlated evidence applies a penalty proportional to O(k^2), with cross-identity attribution preventing dilution. Detection of a managed sybil swarm additionally imposes an exponential capital-loss multiplier, compounding base slashes and asymmetric depreciation. Thus atlas, ivory, and jade accounts gain no cheap majority.
